features.title: Stay with the problem.
features.description: Keep the useful things close. Leave the busywork behind.

items.title: A whole round, neatly organized.
items.body: Separate contest folders and A/B/C problem navigation. Switch problems without losing either solution.

items.title: Your code, your language.
items.body: Independent C++ and Python files, editable starter templates, and your familiar VS Code tooling.

items.title: Tests that tell you something.
items.body: Sample and custom-case tabs, clear pass/fail states, stdout, stderr, and the first differing token.

items.title: Ready when the round starts.
items.body: Add a contest ahead of time. With VS Code running, released problems and samples download automatically.

items.title: Read in your language.
items.body: Use an OpenAI-compatible provider and choose from nine translation languages. Translate on demand or automatically after import; preserve formulas and samples.

items.title: Submit with confidence.
items.body: Optional Codeforces login enables experimental submission with a second confirmation and official-verdict notifications. Copy-and-open is always available.

items.title: Keep an eye on the round.
items.body: View public submissions and rankings, find your position by handle, and keep the contest overview and statements in one tab.

items.title: Reuse AI work locally.
items.body: A general input/output LRU cache shares identical requests. Toggle it and set entry/storage limits; keys stay in secure storage.

workflow.eyebrow: FROM FIRST READ TO FINAL CHECK
workflow.title:
A little less friction.
At every step.

steps.title: Bring your round.
steps.body: Import a contest or a single Codeforces problem, or create a local practice problem. Each collection is separate and shows the newest imports first.

steps.title: Make the solution yours.
steps.body: Read statements and edit in native VS Code. New solutions use your default language and template; optional AI translation uses your chosen model and target language.

steps.title: Test. Refine. Submit.
steps.body: Run samples and custom tests. After Codeforces login, confirm a one-click submission and receive its verdict in a VS Code notification, or copy code to the official submit page.

workflow.notice: Codeforces login and one-click submission are experimental and may be blocked by site verification. Copy-and-open submission remains available without login.

principles.honestBody: This is an early preview. Downloads may encounter site verification; keep the official site available.

items.a: ACStride is a desktop VS Code extension, not a separate editor. Its compatibility identifiers still use cfide.

items.q: Do I need to install Python?
items.a: Only for running Python solutions. Codeforces tools are bundled into the platform-specific VSIX, with no separate CF Tool or downloader installation. C++ solutions require your compiler.

items.q: Can it submit directly to Codeforces?
items.a: Yes, experimentally: log in under Environment checks, select the official compiler and confirm the upload. Exact submissions are monitored for verdict notifications. Site verification may block login or submission; copy-and-open remains available.
Saved code, custom tests, and cached statements remain available. Downloads, rankings, and public submissions require a network connection.

docs.eyebrow: A SHORT PATH TO YOUR FIRST RUN
docs.title: The quick start.
docs.intro: From a fresh installation to a tested solution, without the detour.

sections.title: 01 / Set up your environment
sections.body: Install a matching VSIX and open a trusted local folder. In ACStride Settings → Environment checks, configure C++ and Python tools and run Check all. Login is optional for local work.

sections.title: 02 / Import a contest or problem
sections.body: The sidebar has Contests, Codeforces Problems and Local Practice. Each plus imports or creates an item using your default language. Downloads and bounded retries are automatic; selecting a missing statement starts recovery. Adding a contest does not register you.

sections.title: 03 / Read and write
sections.body: Contests use one editor tab named after the round. Its left rail switches between overview/rankings and problem statements; the header shows ended/countdown status. Standalone problems omit the multi-problem rail. C++ and Python sources remain separate.

sections.title: 04 / Run your cases
sections.body: Use sample tabs or add a custom case with +. Run all saves the selected solution before testing. Compare expected and actual output; local AC is not an official verdict.

sections.title: 05 / Submit with confirmation
sections.body: Log in to Codeforces under Environment checks. One-click submit saves the current code, asks for an official compiler and requires confirmation; verdicts appear as VS Code notifications. Without login, copy code and open the official page. The tracking handle is synced and locked while logged in; otherwise it is editable.

sections.title: 06 / Make it yours
sections.body: Settings has Environment checks, Basic settings, Coding settings and AI assistance tabs. Under Coding, choose the default language, starter templates, tools and local limits. Imports no longer ask for a language; automatic downloads have no per-contest switch.

sections.title: 07 / Translate statements
sections.body: Under AI assistance, set Base URL, model and API Key and test the live connection. Enable translation and choose its target language. Every {{language}} in the English default prompt is replaced before sending; restoring defaults requires confirmation. AI translation is optional and off by default.

sections.title: 08 / Configure AI caching
sections.body: The shared AI input/output LRU defaults to 100 entries and 50 MB. Either limit evicts least recently used requests. Disabling it preserves entries but skips request cache reads/writes; connection tests always contact the provider.

docs.troubleBody: Retry the problem download later. Site verification may block anonymous requests. Existing solutions, custom cases, and cached statements are preserved. Keep the official website as your fallback.

privacy.title: Privacy & licensing.
privacy.intro: This page describes the current early-preview website and extension. It is not a promise about services that have not launched.

sections.title: This website
sections.body: This site has no ACStride account, payment forms, analytics SDK or advertising trackers. The root uses browser language preferences to select a supported URL, with English fallback. Explicit language URLs stay selected. Hosting providers may process access requests and operational logs under their policies.

sections.title: The extension
sections.body: Code, tests and downloaded data stay locally unless you choose an online action. Confirmed one-click submission uploads the current source to Codeforces; copy-and-open writes it to the clipboard. Optional AI translation sends statements and your prompt to your configured provider. API keys use VS Code SecretStorage; the configurable local cache stores AI request input/output, never raw API keys.

sections.title: External services
sections.body: Codeforces login/submission and optional AI requests contact their respective providers directly. Site verification can block Codeforces actions. AI usage may be billed under your provider plan. GitHub, Codeforces, hosting and AI providers apply their own policies; the site and local extension are separate.

sections.title: Licensing
sections.body: The extension has not selected an open-source license; do not assume permission for commercial reuse. The CF Tool development fork retains its upstream MIT license. This website's original code and content are all rights reserved, except for third-party components under their own licenses.

sections.title: Questions
sections.body: For product or privacy questions, open an issue in the extension repository. Do not include passwords, cookies, source code you want to keep private, or other sensitive information in a public issue.
